methodology.anchors: 90-100 market leader · 70-89 strong/production-ready · 50-69 usable but gappy · 30-49 weak/indirect · 0-29 unsupported. Community is log-scale (~16M npm/week → 95; 100k → 70; 1k → 35; <500 → 15-25). CLI scenario favors installable tools; libraries are scored on suitability for building one. Unmeasured performance scores are architecture-based estimates.
methodology.scoring: Scenario score = sum of weight × criterion, rounded half up. Headline = unweighted mean of the five scenario scores; rank = order by headline, as bench/chart.py sorts. Between panels a community criterion moves on the log scale: ΔC = slope × log10(new/old weekly npm downloads), with the slope of the anchor segment the package sits in (25/log10(160) ≈ 11.34 per decade from 100k to ~16M, 17.5 per decade below 100k), held at 95 at or above ~16M. GitHub stars are recorded, not scored. A score without a published breakdown moves by 0.15 × ΔC, rounded half up.
methodology.provenance: 2026-09-26 / 2.2.0 panel. Deuz re-scored against the 2.2.0 release surface, which spans 1.9 → 2.2 since the last panel (chat UI layer, createAgent, SQLite/Redis/Postgres stores, guardrails, handoffs, MCP OAuth, speech/transcription/video, 29 provider ids, native agents, durable and dynamic swarms, leases/drain/recover/cancel on SQLite and Postgres, persistent budgets, evolve, schedules and signals). Competitors: the repo documents no material product change since the 2026-07-22 panel, so every competitor's non-community criteria are carried from it. Community numbers re-fetched live 2026-09-26 (npm downloads API, last-week window 2026-09-18..2026-09-24; GitHub API stars) and moved on the log scale; only Mastra's move changes a rounded score. Earlier panels: 2026-07-22 (1.8.0), 2026-07-20 (1.7.0).

criteria.chatbot: F92 D80 P86 C15 E89 $92 — F+2: speech (OpenAI, ElevenLabs) and transcription (OpenAI, Deepgram) since 2.0 close the speech gap except realtime; SQLite/Redis/Postgres chat, session and memory stores. D+2: 1.9 chat UI layer (ordered parts, writable useChat state, request validation, auto-resume) and ergonomics pass. E+1: store backends, 29 provider ids. Missing: Vue/Svelte, component catalog (2 headless components), realtime voice.
criteria.cli: F80 D75 P84 C15 E88 $90 — F+2: the kit for building one grew (zero-dep node:sqlite stores, MCP stdio + OAuth loopback helpers, resumable native runs, schedules). D+1: 1.9 ergonomics (prompt/instructions, timeout layers, typed tool()). E+2: keyless local Ollama and LM Studio. Still no CLI product; the Node reference sandbox is not production isolation.
criteria.coding: F79 D73 P84 C15 E80 $88 — F+1: workspace sandbox escapes fixed (1.9), doneWhen false-finish guard + createVerifier, evolve's SEARCH/REPLACE patch helpers, idempotent native tools, maxToolResultLength. D+1: typed tool(), per-tool timeouts, unknown tool names self-heal. Gaps unchanged: no first-party git toolset; the Node sandbox is a host child process, not isolation (Docker/E2B are adapters you write).
criteria.asi: F96 D74 P85 C15 E93 $86 — F+2: native agents with explicit outcomes, strict persistence and tool receipts (2.1); swarms that spawn at runtime, blackboards and rounds; leases, drain, recover and cross-process cancel; persistent budgets; schedules and signals (2.2). E+1: SQLite and Postgres backends for swarm, ops and budgets. D held: 1.9 ergonomics offset by two agent engines (native runs reject chat, memory, fallbackModels). Limits: leases are liveness, not safety; external effects need reconciliation; no Redis swarm/ops backend.
criteria.agi: F82 D75 P86 C15 E91 $90 — F+4: speech, transcription and video (2.0) and a swarm product (2.1/2.2) close two of the three gaps named on 1.8; Cohere/Voyage rerankers, evolve. E+1: 21 → 29 provider ids, keyless local hosts. D+1: ergonomics pass. Still missing: realtime voice, MCP server, A2A, provider batch APIs (deferred to 2.3).

scores.delta: -0.4 vs 2026-07-22 (1.8.0): chatbot 77→77, CLI 72→72, coding 71→70, ASI 77→76, AGI 73→73 · rank 9→9 · features up in every scenario; community 23→15 (393 → 141 npm/week) takes back more than they add

notes: Self-assessed by the Deuz maintainers — rubric, criterion breakdowns and sources published for scrutiny; re-derive any score from the anchors.

Deuz community criterion is ONE number (15) applied to every scenario: 141 @deuz-sdk/core npm downloads/week (2026-09-18..24), fetched live 2026-09-26. Log-scale move from 23 at 393/week: 23 + 17.5 × log10(141/393) = 15.2. GitHub stars (2 → 697) and @deuz-sdk/react (198/week) are recorded, not scored — the anchors are npm downloads.

Deuz is scored against the 2.2.0 release commit (40a6f3e, tag v2.2.0); npm still served 2.1.0 at fetch time. The criterion notes cover everything since the 1.8.0 panel: 1.9, 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 (packages/core/CHANGELOG.md, docs/content/docs/reference/whats-new-*.mdx).

Deuz performance and price are held in every scenario. Footprint re-measured for 2.2.0: 10.0 MB installed, 21.9 ms cold import (the 1.8 local pack measured 4.09 MB / 40.3 ms on Node 24.14) — still the smallest install and fastest import in bench/results.json.

Competitors: no material product change is documented in this repo since 2026-07-22, so every competitor's non-community criteria are carried. Without a published breakdown the community move is at most 0.36 of a scenario point (@anthropic-ai/sdk, even ignoring the 95 hold), so those integer scores stand. Mastra's breakdown is published: C 80 → 82 lifts chatbot 75.3 → 75.6 (76) and coding 76.2 → 76.5 (77, half up).

Flagged for the next full panel, not re-scored here: MoonshotAI/kimi-cli is archived in favour of Kimi Code CLI (MoonshotAI/kimi-code); run-llama/LlamaIndexTS is archived (last push 2026-03-11). Vercel's coding breakdown computes to 81.65, not its published 79 — both are carried from 1.8.0 as published.

Honesty check: Deuz stays 9/16 and drops 0.4 to 73.6 — the community criterion takes back more than the 1.9–2.2 features add. Mastra's remote sandboxes (E2B/Daytona) still outrank Deuz's child-process reference sandbox, and Deuz has no CLI product, no git toolset, no Vue/Svelte bindings and no realtime voice.
